title: Accuracy in Estimating Repetitions to Failure During Resistance Exercise
authors: Hackett DA, Cobley SP, Davies TB, Michael SW, Halaki M
journal: Journal of Strength and Conditioning Research
population: 81 adults (53 men and 28 women) with a broad range of resistance training experience, who did the chest press and the leg press. Not runners.
findings: Participants did up to 10 sets of 10 repetitions at 70% of 1RM on the chest press and 80% of 1RM on the leg press. After each set they reported the repetitions they could still do (estimated repetitions to failure, ERF) and then continued to failure to give the actual repetitions to failure (ARF).
The error of ERF differed with ARF (p < 0.001): about 1 repetition when ARF was 0-5 and more than 2 repetitions when ARF was 7-10.

The chest press was estimated more accurately than the leg press: the error was 1 repetition or less for ARF 0-5 on the chest press and for ARF 0-3 on the leg press (p = 0.012). Men were more accurate than women at some ARF values on the leg press (p = 0.008) and not on the chest press.
Resistance training experience did not affect the accuracy of the estimates.
The authors conclude that resistance trainers can estimate repetitions to failure accurately when close to failure and that the estimate could be used to prescribe and monitor resistance exercise.
limitations: Abstract read; the full text is closed access and was not fetched. The abstract gives the size of the error and not its direction. Sets of 10 at 70-80% of 1RM on two machines; sets of 3-6 repetitions and free-weight squats or hinges were not tested. Healthy adults of mixed experience; no runners.
implications: Near the limit of a set (about 5 or fewer repetitions left) the lifter's count is good to about one repetition on a machine, and from 7 or more away it is off by more than two. A reported count of 1-3 is therefore the better-founded end of the scale, and a count of 4 or more (the engine's two-step threshold) is the least reliable. Leg press counts were less accurate than chest press counts.
Training experience did not change the accuracy here, so the engine makes no adjustment for it. Evidence on sets of 3-6 repetitions with a heavy free-weight lift is not in the corpus.
